name: Spain
note: Traveler-focused Spain pack (civil-law, Schengen). Emergencies (112), police/ID, if detained, drugs, street-drinking bans, pickpockets/fake-police scams, driving (IDP + V16 beacon), Schengen 90/180 entry, consular. Verify; not local legal advice.

getLawyer.why: If arrested in Spain, you have the right to a lawyer and an interpreter — ask for both and contact the Embassy of Canada. You can be detained until your identity is confirmed. Sign nothing you don't understand. Dual citizens: if Spain considers you Spanish, consular help may be refused.
Penalties for possession, use, or trafficking are severe — jail or heavy fines. Contact the embassy and get a Spanish lawyer; say and sign nothing without counsel.

deadlines.title: Schengen 90/180 — max 90 days in any 180
deadlines.rule: Canadians need no visa for up to 90 DAYS in any 180-day period across the whole Schengen area (days in any Schengen country count). Passport must be valid at least 3 MONTHS beyond departure. ETIAS will be required once live (apply only on the official EU site). Longer stays need a visa.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Spain

deadlines.title: Drive up to 6 months with a Canadian licence + IDP
deadlines.rule: You may drive up to 6 MONTHS with a valid Canadian licence AND an International Driving Permit (IDP); longer stays need a Spanish licence. Required kit: V16 emergency beacon, reflective jacket inside the car, spare tyre + repair kit, spare bulbs. Low-emission zones may need a permit.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Spain

sentencing.name: Drug possession / trafficking (Spain)
sentencing.first_offender: Possession/use can bring heavy fines; supply/trafficking draws prison.

statutes.title: Carry ID at all times
statutes.summary: Carry your passport or adequate ID at all times — you can be detained until your identity is confirmed. Keep a photocopy/digital copy. Don't hand your passport to anyone except to take details or copy it (watch for fake-police scams — ask for an official badge).

statutes.title: Street-drinking + beachwear + counterfeit bans
statutes.summary: Street drinking is prohibited in Madrid, Barcelona and the Balearic Islands (fines). Some municipalities (incl. Barcelona) ban beachwear off the beach (on-the-spot fines). Buying counterfeit goods from street vendors is illegal in some municipalities (heavy fines for tourists). Photographing military installations is illegal.

statutes.act: Convention on the Transfer of Sentenced Persons
statutes.title: Consular access + prisoner transfer
statutes.summary: Consular officials can help if you're arrested but cannot interfere in Spanish judicial matters. Canada and Spain allow a sentenced Canadian to request transfer to a Canadian prison (both must agree; slow; not guaranteed). Dual citizenship is not recognized.

book.title: Police, ID, and your rights in Spain
book.overview: Spain is a civil-law EU/Schengen country. Carry ID at all times — you can be detained until your identity is confirmed. If arrested you have the right to a lawyer and an interpreter; ask for both and contact the Embassy of Canada. Emergency: 112. Watch for fake-police scams — ask any plainclothes officer for an official badge.
your_rights: Right to a lawyer and an interpreter if detained.
Right to contact the Embassy of Canada.
You can ask any officer (esp. plainclothes) for an official ID badge.
You can be detained until identity is confirmed — carry ID.
Do not sign anything you don't understand.
key_steps: Carry your passport/ID and a copy.
If stopped by plainclothes 'police', ask to see an official badge.
If detained: ask for a lawyer, an interpreter, and the embassy.
Report theft to get a 'denuncia' for insurance.
common_mistakes: Handing a passport to a fake-police scammer.
Signing Spanish documents you don't understand.
Assuming dual citizenship gets Canadian consular help.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately on arrest — ask for a lawyer, an interpreter, and the embassy.

book.title: Entry to Spain — Schengen 90/180 and ETIAS
book.overview: Canadians can stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area with no visa. Passport must be valid 3+ months beyond departure. The EU Entry/Exit System (EES) collects your facial image and fingerprints; ETIAS will be required once live (official EU site only). Longer stays need a visa.
your_rights: Visa-free up to 90 days in any 180 (Schengen-wide).
You're entitled to entry once requirements are met.
Dual citizens of an ETIAS country must use that European passport.
key_steps: Count your Schengen days (all Schengen countries count).
Check passport validity (3+ months beyond departure).
Apply for ETIAS on the official EU site once live.
For stays over 90 days, get a visa in advance.
common_mistakes: Applying for ETIAS on a scam site.
Forgetting days in other Schengen countries count.
book.when_lawyer: For overstays, visa refusals, or removal, consult a Spanish immigration lawyer.

book.title: Laws that catch tourists off guard in Spain
book.overview: Drugs carry severe penalties. Street drinking is banned in Madrid, Barcelona and the Balearics (fines). Some cities fine beachwear worn off the beach and buying counterfeit goods from street vendors. Photographing military sites is illegal. Carrying €10,000+ needs a customs declaration.
your_rights: Presumption of innocence; right to a lawyer and interpreter.
key_steps: Don't drink alcohol in the street in Madrid/Barcelona/Balearics.
Cover up off the beach where required.
Don't buy counterfeit goods from street vendors.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately for any charge — a Spanish criminal lawyer and the embassy.

book.title: Pickpockets, scams, and staying safe in Spain
book.overview: Emergency: 112. Pickpocketing and bag-snatching are common in Madrid and Barcelona (transit hubs, airports, car-rental desks, hotel lobbies, beaches, tourist sites). Watch for fake-police, staged-breakdown road scams, and drink spiking. Demonstrations occur regularly (esp. Catalonia).
your_rights: The embassy has a 24/7 Emergency Watch & Response line.
You can file a 'denuncia' (police report) for insurance.
key_steps: Keep valuables secure at transit hubs and tourist sites.
Ask plainclothes 'police' for an official badge.
Accept roadside help only from uniformed National Police/Civil Guard.
Never leave food/drinks unattended; avoid crowds at protests.
After theft, file a denuncia (translator line 902 102 112, weekdays).
common_mistakes: Leaving valuables in a parked car.
Not getting a denuncia for insurance.
book.when_lawyer: For a serious crime against you, the embassy can refer local lawyers.
